story_type: sinking pleasure boat offshore, swimmer lowered to the deck, basket load to the boat
hook: Sinking twenty miles out, with four people aboard.
narration: This boat was sinking twenty miles off Galveston Island, with four people aboard.
At about eight twenty four that morning, the owner made a mayday call.
The pleasure craft No Problem was taking on water, in danger of going under.
A Coast Guard helicopter crew from Air Station Houston lowered a rescue swimmer to the boat.
Coast Guard aircrews can lower a portable pump to a flooding boat, so the people aboard can push the water back out.
Then the crew sent the rescue basket down to the boat.
outcome: The Coast Guard and good Samaritans saved the sinking boat with all four people aboard.
title: Boat sinking 20 miles off Galveston
description:
On Nov. 20, 2010, the Coast Guard and good Samaritans helped save the sinking pleasure craft No Problem and its four passengers about 20 miles off Galveston Island, Texas.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer Richard Brahm, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/101072/coast-guard-good-samaritans-save-sinking-vessel

drop_reason: QA Nov 7: soft, washed out 2010 footage; the boat never looks like it is sinking (it sits level while a pump case is lowered), line 6 promises a basket the footage never shows, and sinking-boat stories already ran twice this week (Cape Fear, nose first). No edit fixes the missing danger.
